input.summary: Full source-fidelity preflight completed against input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (the only affirmative inventor authority); input/brief.md was used only for title, applicant/inventor, no-priority, and no-government-support formalities, and the YOU passage in conversation.md (which speaks of a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface") was treated as non-authority and correctly appears nowhere in the draft. Every claim limitation in all seventeen claims (independent claims 1, 11, 14 and dependent claims 2-10, 12-13, 15-17) was traced to an exact affirmative disclosure passage: two semicircular frame halves with hinge at one end and releasable latch at the other; three circumferentially distributed jaw carriages each sliding in a radial guide and carrying a pivoting concave jaw pad that bears without a tool-specific pipe diameter; a segmented cam ring retained in an annular guide with one segment carried by each frame half; complementary hinge-end and latch-end drive faces that couple the segments on frame closure and separate on opening; followers in respective oblique slots converting limited-stroke ring rotation into synchronized inward carriage travel; a wedge on the latch bearing on a ring drive face; outward-biasing carriage springs that retract the jaws on release before the halves are opened; the first holding position and second over-center clamping position; the force-limiting spring stack between latch handle and wedge absorbing travel remaining after all pads contact the pipe rather than forcing one jaw farther; the indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range while reporting load and not diameter; and the mounting boss outside the annular guide supporting a sensor, tool or conduit and not participating in jaw synchronization. Claim 6's "same inward travel at every jaw carriage" and the description's synchronization statements trace to "translate that rotation into synchronized inward travel of all three jaw carriages"; claim 11's installed-assembly class and claim 14/16 method steps trace to the disclosed installation and removal sequences. All twenty-eight numerals in draft/numerals.md (10-26, 30-66) were checked: each carries exactly one meaning across the description, the claims and every figure brief, each is used in the description, each appears on at least one figure, and no numeral is reused for a second part - notably the junction drive faces 44/46/48/50 are kept lexically distinct from the ring drive face 54 in both the description and the claims. Each of FIG. 1 through FIG. 6 was compared against draft/07-drawings.md and the detailed description; the six Brief Description entries match their briefs and each figure cited in the description contains the numerals attributed to it. No section lines are designated in any view, so the repeated-designation check passes vacuously. Figure geometry was tested against the functional-surface standard: the wedge taper direction, slot lean sense, drive-face depth, runout, angle and radial/circumferential end positions are nowhere verbalized; FIG. 3's positioning of ring drive face 54 is expressly a leader-collision convention conveying no circumferential relationship and is confined to the figure brief, with FIG. 6 repeating only that same convention; and no "by way of example", "any closed outline" or similar shape-justifying language appears in the application text, Brief Description or claims. FIG. 5's spring "acting between the carriage and the frame" with a radial line of action was judged inherent in the disclosed carriage that "slides in a radial guide" and the disclosed "spring biases each carriage outward", and the application text itself asserts no anchoring; FIG. 1's and FIG. 2's mounting-boss placements are non-substantive page placements of an affirmatively disclosed part. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced to the disclosure, as instructed, and assert no invention matter. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains in any draft file, terminology is uniform between claims, summary, abstract and description, claim antecedent bases resolve, no means-plus-function language is used, and the cross-reference and government-support sections match the brief's no-priority, no-federal-funding instructions. The complete claims, numbered parts, figure briefs and drawing descriptions, and affirmative inventor sources were all checked and traced without an unsupported technical assertion.

content.text:
I reviewed every input file, all ten draft sections, the numeral ledger, and all six figure briefs, and built a full source ledger tracing each claim limitation, numbered part, and figure-brief geometry statement back to the disclosure.

Ledger highlights (all traced to affirmative USER text in `input/disclosure.md`):

- **Claims 1–17**: three jaw carriages in radial guides, pivoting concave jaw pads, carriage springs biasing outward, segmented cam ring in an annular guide with one segment per frame half, complementary hinge-end and latch-end drive faces coupled by frame closure, followers in oblique slots, wedge on the latch bearing a ring drive face, limited stroke, force-limiting spring stack between handle and wedge, indicator pin vs. fixed edge at a predetermined compression range, first/over-center latch positions, mounting boss outside the annular guide (non-synchronizing), and the install/release method sequence — each has an exact source sentence.
- **Numerals 10–66**: each appears in at least one figure and in the description, each designates exactly one part, and the chain FIG. 1 (12 upper / 14 lower, hinge left, latch right) → FIG. 3 (32 upper / 34 lower) → FIG. 6 (44/46 at the left = hinge-end junction, 48/50 at the right = latch-end junction) is internally consistent.
- **Figure briefs**: the only appearance choices not dictated by the source — the mounting-boss page placement in FIG. 1 and the circumferential position of the ring drive face in FIGS. 3 and 6 — are marked "shown schematically", are justified solely as leader/visibility conventions, expressly disclaim any circumferential relationship, and stay confined to the figure briefs. The application text and Brief Description remain shape-neutral and contain no "by way of example" or "any closed outline" broadening. Under the stated rule these remain depiction conventions rather than invention assertions.
- No drafting notes, placeholders, open questions, or unresolved alternatives remain; the drafting agent's stray "microsuction/self-adhering layer" prose in `conversation.md` is a YOU passage and does not appear anywhere in the draft.

No verified defects to report.

input.summary: Full preflight completed against input/disclosure.md as sole invention authority, with input/brief.md used only for title, applicant/inventor, priority and government-support formalities, and with the YOU passage in input/conversation.md (which stray-references a "self-adhering layer with a microsuction surface") treated as context only and confirmed absent from the draft. A complete source ledger was built and every item traced. Claims: all 17 claims (independent 1, 11, 14 and dependents 2-10, 12-13, 15-17) were traced limitation by limitation — two semicircular frame halves with hinge at one end and releasable latch at the other; three circumferentially distributed jaw carriages slidable in respective radial guides; pivoting concave jaw pads that bear without a tool-specific pipe diameter; a carriage spring biasing each carriage outward and retracting the jaws on release; a cam ring retained in an annular guide for a limited-stroke rotation; first and second cam-ring segments each carried by and staying with its own frame half; complementary hinge-end and latch-end drive faces that engage on closure to couple the segments and separate on opening; a follower per carriage received in a respective oblique slot inclined to the circumferential direction and advancing all carriages inward together by the same travel; a wedge carried by the latch bearing on a ring drive face; a force-limiting spring stack in the drive path between latch handle and wedge that absorbs remaining travel without advancing one pad farther than the others; the first (holding) and second over-center latch positions; the indicator pin moving relative to a fixed edge of the latch housing at a predetermined compression range; the mounting boss outside the annular guide supporting a sensor, tool or conduit and not participating in synchronization; and the install/release method steps. Each maps to an exact affirmative disclosure sentence, so no dependent-claim limitation or optional embodiment is untraced. Numerals and numbered parts: all 28 ledger entries (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 20, 22, 24, 26, 30-42, 44-66) were checked — every numeral appears in at least one figure brief and in the detailed description, every numeral designates exactly one part, no numeral in any figure is missing from the ledger or the description, and no ledger entry is orphaned. Claim vocabulary and description vocabulary match exactly (releasable latch, jaw carriage, radial guide, jaw pad, cam ring, cam-ring segment, annular guide, oblique slot, follower, carriage spring, hinge-end and latch-end drive faces, wedge, ring drive face, latch handle, latch housing, fixed edge, force-limiting spring stack, indicator pin, mounting boss), and the ring drive face 54 is kept terminologically distinct from the segment-coupling drive faces 44/46/48/50. Figure briefs and drawing descriptions: FIGS. 1-6 were compared against the Brief Description of the Drawings and the detailed description; the orientation chain is consistent (first frame half 12 upper and second 14 lower in FIG. 1; first cam-ring segment 32 upper and second 34 lower in FIG. 3; hinge-end faces 44/46 at the left junction and latch-end faces 48/50 at the right junction in FIG. 6, matching the hinge-left/latch-right arrangement of FIG. 1), and every depicted structure — pipe, annular frame with upper and lower halves, hinge, latch with lever arm, three carriages, concave pads, mounting boss, cam ring in its annular guide, three oblique slots, two junctions with complementary drive faces, wedge, spring stack, indicator pin and housing edge, carriage spring, follower — is source-disclosed. No section line is designated in any view, so no section-designation mismatch exists; the FIG. 2 "near-side frame material omitted" and FIG. 4 "near side of the housing removed" cutaways are described identically in the brief and in section 07. The only appearance choices not dictated by the source are the page placement of the mounting boss in FIG. 1 and the circumferential position of the ring drive face in FIGS. 3 and 6; both are labeled "shown schematically", are justified solely as leader-clearance and separate-visibility conventions, expressly disclaim any circumferential relationship to the slots or junctions, and are confined to the figure briefs. The application text, Brief Description and claims remain shape-neutral and contain no "by way of example", "any closed outline", or other broadening added to justify a renderer choice, so these remain depiction conventions rather than invention assertions. No drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative or internal comment remains anywhere in the draft, the abstract is 146 words, no means-plus-function language is used, and the title, "Not applicable" cross-reference and "Not applicable" government-support statement match the filing brief. Background prior-art characterizations were not traced to inventor sources, as instructed, and no prior_art files were part of this material. The complete claims, numerals and numbered parts, figure briefs and drawing descriptions, and affirmative inventor sources were all checked and traced with no unsupported technical assertion and no internal inconsistency found.
